title: Weighted MaxSAT by implicit hitting sets (MaxHS)
description: Weighted MaxSAT with the implicit hitting set loop of MaxHS (Davies and Bacchus): an optimal hitting set of the cores found so far, then a SAT oracle on the clauses it keeps. The check looks for a witness; a failed check is refined by its unsat core (G.core), and each core is relaxed (for a in C.core: E = E.without(a)) so that one round can find several disjoint cores. Each core is made subset-minimal first (C.core.minimal): on the example the loop needs 5 rounds instead of 57 (the variant plain-cores). track draws the lower bound (the hitting set's cost) and the upper bound (the witness's cost) in the Statistics tab until they meet. One solution: an optimal set of soft clauses to give up.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% The instance (Instances tab): soft(C,W) is a soft clause C with weight W, hard(C) a hard
% clause; pos(C,V) and neg(C,V) are the literals of clause C.
cl(C) :- soft(C,_).
cl(C) :- hard(C).
var(V) :- pos(_,V).
var(V) :- neg(_,V).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% The hitting-set solver: which soft clauses to give up (drop). It knows nothing of the
% formula; it only learns the cores, as clauses "drop at least one clause of this core".
{ drop(C) : soft(C,_) }.
% Each call is optimal (A.solve(optimal)): the cheapest set that hits every core so far.
% Its cost is a lower bound on the optimum.
#minimize { W,C : drop(C), soft(C,W) }.
#show drop/1.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% The SAT oracle: an assignment that satisfies the hard clauses and every soft clause that is
% not dropped. It is a witness: if it exists, the hitting set is optimal; if not, the unsat
% core names the soft clauses (assumed not dropped) that cannot all hold.
{ t(V) } :- var(V).
sat(C) :- pos(C,V), t(V).
sat(C) :- neg(C,V), not t(V).
:- hard(C), not sat(C).
:- soft(C,_), not drop(C), not sat(C).
% Not needed for correctness: with it, X.cost is the true cost of the witness X, an upper bound.
#minimize { W,C : soft(C,W), not sat(C) }.
#show t/1.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Implicit hitting sets (MaxHS): an optimal hitting set of the cores found so far, then a SAT
# call with the clauses it keeps. Unsatisfiable: a new core, which the next hitting set must
# hit. Satisfiable: the hitting set is optimal. Within a round, each core is relaxed
# (E.without) and the oracle is asked again, so that one round finds several disjoint cores.
# Each core is made subset-minimal first (C.core.minimal): a short core is a strong clause.
# The variant plain-cores uses the cores as clasp returns them.
upper = none
loop:
    M = A.solve(optimal)
    if not M: stop "the hard clauses are unsatisfiable"
    track lower = M.cost
    E = G(M)
    cores = 0
    loop:
        X = C.solve(assume E)
        if X:
            if upper == none or X.cost < upper: upper = X.cost
            break
        K = C.core.minimal             # no assumption of it can be left out
        if K.on(G).size == 0: stop "the hard clauses are unsatisfiable"
        A.add(K.on(G))                 # hit at least one clause of the core
        cores = cores + 1
        count cores
        for a in K:                    # relax the core's clauses, look for a disjoint one
            E = E.without(a)
    track upper = upper
    if cores == 0:
        log "optimum:", M.cost
        accept M
        stop

variants.name: plain-cores
variants.loop:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Implicit hitting sets (MaxHS): an optimal hitting set of the cores found so far, then a SAT
# call with the clauses it keeps. Unsatisfiable: a new core, which the next hitting set must
# hit. Satisfiable: the hitting set is optimal. Within a round, each core is relaxed
# (E.without) and the oracle is asked again, so that one round finds several disjoint cores.
upper = none
loop:
    M = A.solve(optimal)
    if not M: stop "the hard clauses are unsatisfiable"
    track lower = M.cost
    E = G(M)
    cores = 0
    loop:
        X = C.solve(assume E)
        if X:
            if upper == none or X.cost < upper: upper = X.cost
            break
        K = C.core.on(G)               # the core's soft clauses, as a clause for A
        if K.size == 0: stop "the hard clauses are unsatisfiable"
        A.add(K)                       # hit at least one clause of the core
        cores = cores + 1
        count cores
        for a in C.core:               # relax the core's clauses, look for a disjoint one
            E = E.without(a)
    track upper = upper
    if cores == 0:
        log "optimum:", M.cost
        accept M
        stop
